problem: Bare-HF off-diagonal couplings between singly excited CSFs are inconsistent with the DFT-derived response used by their diagonal ROKS energies. Glyoxal mixes two orthogonal single excitations with a bare coupling of 2.741 eV.
correction: I=fully_symmetric(C+S), I_atom=I on quartets whose four Lowdin AOs share an atom and zero otherwise. C_prime=C-(I+I_atom)/2; S_prime=S-(I-I_atom)/2. No adjustable weight. Preserve original native diagonal and four-spin blocks as in the parent SI functional.
primary_ground_reference: Stationary-ground projected SI: Q=1-|g><g|, with the independently stationary ground functional energy and its complete moving-projector response. Do not reference or fit the auxiliary SI ground correlation lowering.
controls: retain both full SI eigenvalue minus stationary ground and conventional full-SI ground-referenced gaps
implementation_scope: first an operator audit with explicit small TDA matrices; a successful implementation must contract response on the few CSF transition vectors without diagonalizing or constructing a full TDA matrix
development: All eleven previous predictions and labels are exposed development; no claim of blind validation
reason: Preserve the one-center atomic spin blocks, the native tight-binding spin-polarization degrees of freedom, while using the minimum-change charge/spin completion between centers. This introduces orbital-locality dependence without classifying transitions or fitting excitation energies.
previous_diagnostic: Earlier PBE0/M06 CASCI projection used raw Hamiltonian diagonals, different anchors and unoptimized states; those spectra were poor. This is a separate native-orbital CAM response/off-diagonal-only control with exact ROKS diagonal residuals.
